summary: Intermittent NVLink/PCIe IO "sputter" causing deferred batch buildup and autoscaler oscillation in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Midday we observed a gradual throughput degradation and p99 latency growth for a NimbleTranslate dedicated pool. Traffic pattern unchanged; the autoscaler started oscillating (add/remove cycles) and many short batched requests were deferred for several seconds before execution.
Impact: Customer requests hit p99 latencies of 8–12s and observed occasional 5xx spikes; downstream SLA alerts triggered.
Environment: Dedicated capacity (pool-id: pool-nimble-az1), region us-east, GPU type: A100-40GB with NVLink, serving-runtime v2.8.3, autoscaler v1.4.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Replay NimbleTranslate midday traffic pattern via load-test (small short streams + bursts). 2) Watch allocator attach rates + NVLink error metrics. 3) Observe autoscaler decisions and slot attach/detach events.
Observed behavior: - At ~12:05 UTC we saw short intermittent NVLink/PCIe completion delays (what we label as "sputter") lasting 100–400ms at 1–2 minute cadence. - These delays caused the internal batcher to push several small batches into deferred state; deferred queue length grew from 0 to ~200 in 7 minutes. - Autoscaler interpreted elevated queue length as capacity shortage and tried to add nodes; new nodes attached but their initial attach throughput was low because the same IO sputter persisted, leading to quick scale-downs. - End result: autoscaler oscillation (add -> remove -> add) for ~20 minutes and a net throughput reduction.
Relevant metrics/logs: - nvlink_err_count spiked in short bursts (see graph link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/xyz/nvlink-errors). - pci_io_completion_ms 95th jumped from 12ms -> 380ms intermittently. - Allocator logs show repeated attach timeouts followed by retries: "attach_slot(timeout) -> retry". - Autoscaler decisions: add-node at 12:08, remove-node at 12:11, add-node at 12:13 (see autoscaler audit: https://logs.redwood/auto/2026-03-10/12).
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered: 1) Noisy tenant saturating NVLink lanes (some tenant performing heavy allreduce-like IO). 2) Hardware-level PCIe switch hiccups causing transient completion latency. 3) Driver-level regression in CUDA/NVML that surfaces under mixed short-stream workloads.
Quick checks performed: - Correlated tenant IDs with NVLink spikes; found tenant tx-778 (internal analytics) had a burst of small heavy-IO jobs coincident with incidents. - SRE run 'nvlink-reset' on one host: transient improvement observed for ~15m. - Driver rolling window: no recent driver upgrades in that zone in past 48h. - Kernel dmesg on one affected host shows occasional 'PCIe completion timeout' warnings at time of spikes.
Current working theory: combination of a noisy tenant causing periodic NVLink fanout plus a hardware PCIe completion sensitivity causing IO completion tail. This combination magnifies deferred-batching behavior and misleads autoscaler heuristics.
Investigation owners: Diego (SRE), Lina Chen (infra).
workarounds_and_next_steps:
Immediate mitigations (in-progress): 1) Triage noisy tenant: asked customer and platform to throttle/limit tx-778 analytics batch window; SRE applied soft throttling on that tenant for 30m. 2) Temporarily widen autoscaler hysteresis: bump scale-up cool-down to 3m and scale-down window to 8m for pool-nimble-az1 to avoid rapid churn. 3) Isolate affected hosts: schedule workloads away from hosts that show persistent PCIe warnings.
Follow-ups: - Replace suspect PCIe switch hardware on two hosts (ticketed with infra vendor). - Add NVLink/pci IO tail alerts and enrich autoscaler heuristics to ignore short transient IO spikes under X seconds.
Owner: Diego Ramos. ETA for vendor replacement: 2026-03-16.
